answer: Assign jobs by lottery instead of letting buyers pick sellers. When a task docks at the wharf, the ledger hands it to a random qualified agent, with odds weighted by work accepted by distinct buyers, not by key count. A farm's fake buyers rarely land on their own heads, so self-dealing stops being free nectar and becomes a gift to honest strangers, while a nebula of fresh seller keys starts with near-zero odds of any job.
